podcast.title: Early 1950s Success
podcast.body: Johnny Ray achieved a string of hits in the very early 1950s in the US, with his biggest hits coming in 1951. His main period of success in the UK was 1956 to 1958. "in the US, his biggest hits came in 1951, and he had a string of hits in the very early 50s."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 97: "Song to Woody" by Bob Dylan

podcast.title: Influence on Bob Dylan
podcast.body: Ray's music was the first to captivate a young Robert Zimmerman (Bob Dylan), though music historian Clinton Heylin incorrectly suggested Dylan might have confused him with Johnny Ace, mistaking the timeline of Ray's US and UK success. "He was first captivated by Johnny Ray."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 97: "Song to Woody" by Bob Dylan

podcast.title: Managed by Al Green (Mobster)
podcast.body: Johnny Ray was one of the biggest names in Whitepop music at the time and was managed by local mobster Al Green. "He managed Johnny Ray, one of the biggest names in Whitepop music at the time."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty-Four: "Reet Petite" by Jackie Wilson

podcast.title: UK Tour Requirement (Early 1950s)
podcast.body: When Johnny Ray toured the UK in the early 1950s, he was required to employ British musicians as a condition of performing, due to the mutual protectionist agreement between the American and British musicians' unions. "Similarly, when Johnny Ray had toured the UK in the early 50s, he'd had to employ British musicians."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
